answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with adversarial strategy tournaments: each epoch, every head is randomly paired against non-kin strangers in a zero-sum game, and only the score counts toward standing. A sybil farm can mint an island of heads, but it cannot play them all — one scripted strategy deployed N times is countered by strangers who exploit its tell, like a single juniper's shadow copied across a field. Diversifying play costs real inference per head, and each pigment of strategy must be genuinely earned. The farm's edge dies when winning costs labor per head.
